title: Hebrews Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Hebrews 5: what a high priest is appointed to do, the priest after the order of Melchizedek, and milk against solid food.

questions.text: What is every high priest appointed to offer, according to verse 1?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says every high priest is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.

questions.text: Why can the high priest deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says he can deal gently with them because he himself is also surrounded with weakness.

answers.text: Because the law commands him to be kind
Because the people chose him for the office
Because he has never gone astray himself
Because he himself is also surrounded with weakness

questions.text: Who is named as the example of someone called by God to this honor?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.

questions.text: Which words does the text say were spoken to Christ about being made a high priest?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says Christ did not glorify himself, but it was he who said to him, "You are my Son. Today I have become your father."

answers.text: You shall lead my people out of Egypt
You are the shepherd of all the nations
You are my Son. Today I have become your father
Today you will stand before kings

questions.text: After whose order does the text say he is a priest forever?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 quotes: "You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek."

questions.text: What did he offer up in the days of his flesh, according to verse 7?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says that in the days of his flesh he offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death.

answers.text: Prayers and petitions, with strong crying and tears
Bulls and goats on the altar of the temple
Bread and wine before all the people
Gold and incense brought from far away

questions.text: What does verse 8 say the Son learned by the things which he suffered?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says that though he was a Son, he yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.

questions.text: Having been made perfect, to whom did he become the author of eternal salvation?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says that having been made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation to all of those who obey him.

answers.text: To the priests of the order of Levi
To all of those who obey him
To those who were born in Israel

questions.text: What does the writer say the readers have come to need?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says that although by this time they should be teachers, they have come to need milk, and not solid food.

questions.text: For whom is solid food, according to verse 14?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.

answers.text: For those who are babies in the faith
For those who are full grown
For those who have just been taught
